pr.title: Color requests by theme, put start first, and offer Looks good and There's an issue
pr.head: e35a3a600160d2f6cea6e5b17740e8013c38ffe8

summary: Projector's panel sits above the Claude Code prompt and lists your pull requests and your inbox. The inbox holds three kinds of item that agents post: a question wants an answer, a notice wants a read, and a request asks you to do something only you can do, such as testing a build on your phone. Each open item's line has its own color, so you can tell the kinds apart at a glance. Opening an item shows its drawer, with numbered buttons you press by digit, by click, or by Enter.
This pull request reworks how requests look and how you finish them:

• Color. A request's line used Claude Code's suggestion color, which every built-in theme draws in the same blue as a question. It is now a pastel peach, rgb(255,190,140), on the dark themes, and a darker orange, rgb(180,90,40), on light and light-daltonized, where the peach was too faint to read.
  • Start first. A request with a start action (something the agent prepares before you begin, such as installing the build) offers Start, or Retry after the agent reports it was blocked, on 1, ahead of the other choices.
  • Two ways to say done. Looks good and There's an issue replace Done and Declined. Both mark the request done, and the words you chose are recorded as the outcome's text, so the agent knows to look for a failure.
  • Decline as an action. decline request on 8 takes dismiss's place and declines at once.

The agents block that project init writes into each repository's AGENTS.md moves to version 21, so agents know the new words. The review found one open problem: the new state key is not declared in hooks/types.d.ts, so claude plugin validate . and hooks/typecheck.sh fail.

groups.title: What a sent prompt records
groups.kicker: The words under a quoted request, and the outcome each records
intro: When you press a choice, the panel puts the quoted request and the choice's words in your prompt. Sending it records the outcome. CHOICES lists the two choices, Looks good and There's an issue. readPrompt reads the first line under a quote as the outcome when it is one of those words, or a plain Done or Declined typed by hand. Each outcome it returns now carries the word that said so, and the panel passes a choice's words to project inbox done as --text.
The request tool's description, and the result it returns, now tell the agent that both choices mean done and that a decline arrives as a DECLINED message.

files.note: Replaces OUTCOMES with CHOICES and a map of the words that resolve a request, and updates the request tool's description.
Covers each choice, a typed Done and Declined, and the new word field.

groups.title: The panel's request line and drawer
groups.kicker: Color by theme, Start first, the choices, and decline on 8
intro: paint already chose the panel's background from the Claude Code theme, following a custom theme to the built-in theme it builds on. It now also sets themeRequestColor: rgb(180,90,40) for light and light-daltonized, and peach for any other theme. The item line and the collapsed + N requests line both read it through kindColors.

In the drawer, startOf decides whether the first button is Start, Retry, or absent, and the two choices follow it. A resolved request marks the choice it was recorded with. A done request recorded from a terminal or with a typed Done, or a declined one, gets a Done or Declined line of its own. decline request uses the line dismiss uses for other items, so it acts at once, and the declined request is struck through and offers restore request.

Pressing Start still goes through act, which passes the start action the drawer shows as --action. The CLI refuses that with exit 65 when the agent has revised the action, and the panel then reads the store again.

groups.title: The agents block, version 21
groups.kicker: What Projector tells every agent about a request's outcome
intro: project init writes a block of instructions into each repository's AGENTS.md from src/projector/templates/agents-block.md. Each version of that template is pinned by its hash in tests/test_instructions.py, so a text change needs a new version. Version 21 names the two choices, says that a decline arrives as DECLINED, and tells an agent to find out what failed when the person says There's an issue.

checks.text: The block in AGENTS.md matches the rendered template (block_matches returns true). The template's SHA-256 is the pinned 88a3ad16…, and no template line is longer than 79 columns.
The completed inbox/requests plan still describes Done and Declined. AGENTS.md leaves completed plans as they are and keeps docs/ current instead.
